Q: Is there a way to plot groups with a single row as filled symbols in a boxplot using ggplot? A:

Instead of filtering your data you can use an if_else to conditionally remove the boxes and/or points based on the number of observations.

library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr, warn = FALSE)

pd <- position_dodge2(preserve = "single", width = .75)

example |>
  add_count(
    family, status
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(y = eq, x = family)) +
  geom_boxplot(
    aes(
      fill = status,
      linewidth = I(if_else(n == 1, 0, .5))
    ),
    outlier.size = 3,
    outlier.shape = 21,
    position = pd
  ) +
  stat_summary(
    geom = "point",
    aes(
      fill = status,
      size = I(if_else(n == 1, 3, 0))
    ),
    fun = median,
    shape = 21,
    position = pd
  )

Q: How much swap does a nockchain node need? A:

64 GB of RAM is ideal.

If you have 32 GB of RAM, use 32 GB of SWAP as well.

Q: How to end or fail AWS Glue job with error? A:

This is written as pyspark, as it's what I know

args = getResolvedOptions(
   sys.argv, ["TempDir", "JOB_NAME"]
)
job = Job(glue_context)
job.init(args["JOB_NAME"], args)

if my_check() == False:
    # you can use any other exit code and glue will still report failure
    # because the job is not committed
    sys.exit(0)

do_normal_stuff()
job.commit()

The spark job and glue job are different things, which is why you can't interchange their IDs.

Q: The value provided for the report parameter '' is not valid for its type. (rsReportParameterTypeMismatch) A:

Probably incorrect Date format on the server. To resolve it, change the Date format on the host to en-us via Control Panel
